title: Neural data analysis
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to analyze the data neuroscientists record, in Python: spike trains and firing rates, peristimulus time histograms and raster data, tuning curves, spike-train statistics and the Poisson model, correlations between neurons, local field potentials and the Fourier transform, power spectra and filtering, calcium imaging traces, encoding models, population decoding, and dimensionality reduction of neural populations.
primary_reading: Case Studies in Neural Data Analysis by Kramer and Eden, Python edition (free online)

weeks.1: Spike trains, rasters and firing rates
weeks.4: Spike-train statistics and the Poisson model
weeks.6: Local field potentials and the Fourier transform
weeks.8: Calcium imaging traces and spike inference
weeks.9: Encoding models: linear–nonlinear and Poisson regression

blocks.deliverable: Compute a PSTH from supplied spike times.
Fit a tuning curve and test a Poisson assumption.
Compute a cross-correlogram from two spike trains.
Week 7 midterm; compute the power spectrum of a supplied signal.
Decode a stimulus from supplied population responses.
Find the main dimensions of a supplied population recording.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Data analysis report: analyze a small supplied data set of spike times recorded during a task, in plain Python written without analysis libraries for the core steps, computing rasters, firing rates, tuning curves and a simple decoder, and write a report that states each result with its uncertainty and what it does and does not show about the neurons.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
